summary: Our project is an interactive educational game designed to teach children from the age of 7 to 12 about the challenges of managing a lunar outpost. Through a gaming experience while exploring the difficulties of living on the moon.
details:
What did we develop?

We developed an educational video game designed for children. The game simulates the challenges of managing a lunar outpost, allowing players to explore different scientific problems while exploring and surviving with limited energy.

How does it solve the challenge?

Our project attacks a real-world problem of introducing the problems of the lunar outpost to younger audiences. By transforming complex concepts into a simple videogame with an enjoyable experience.

Why is it important?

It is important because it encourages the children’s interest in STEM and at the same time introduces them to real challenges that future astronauts will be facing.

What does it do?

The game allows players to manage a lunar base, monitor the system and energy, maintain energy supplies, grow food and some environmental problems.

How does it work?

Players must survive while managing limited resources and maintaining their lunar base in a good state. Players can use a monitor screen to check the status and eat to recover energy.

What benefits does it have?

The game promotes scientific curiosity, critical thinking and resource management. It also provides an introduction to a lunar outpost and as we have said before it encourages children´s interest in Science and Space.

What tools, coding language, or hardware did you use?

During the development of this project we used several digital tools and software programs. Such as, Paint, Canva, Google Docs, Blender, Visual Studio Community and Godot .NET. Our main programming language was C#, which we used to develop the game’s main functions. And regarding hardware, we used Laptops, Desktop Computers and Ipads.

Did we use AI tools? 

Yes, we used artificial intelligence tools. Such as Claude or Chat GPT to assist us during the creation of the code (We mainly used them to correct errors). As these tools served as additional support throughout development. While our team worked hard in the game.
